newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek FRNs fall, rates rise further on soft drachma.
newsitem.headline: Greek FRNs fall, rates rise further on soft drachma.

text.p: Greek floaters due 2002 and 2003 came under selling pressure around mid-session, shedding half a point, as depos and forex forwards rose further in response to the drachma's weakness against the ecu, dealers said.
"There is selling of FRNs from abroad," said a bond dealer from a private bank. "Prices of FRNs due 2002 and 2003 have lost half a point so far and fixed coupon bonds are soft."
Money market dealers pointed to the drachma's weakness against the ecu and likely forex outflows at the fixing to explain a further spike in depo and implied drachma rates from forex forwards.
"Depos and forex forwards have firmed more on drachma selling for ecus from abroad," said a dealer. "We will be awaiting to see what is going to happen at today's fixing."
The drachma was trading close to its intraday high of 310.10/15 against the ecu, dealers said.
"London-based banks have sold a large amount of drachmas for ecus, driving ecu/drachma above 310," said a forex dealer. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
